title: Ecma International-relevant MDN issues
description: Issue filed on MDN Web Docs related to pages attached to technologies developed by Ecma International

items.content_html:
MDN URL

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/parseInt#description

What specific section or headline is this issue about?

Description

What information was incorrect, unhelpful, or incomplete?

One of the paragraphs reads:

If parseInt encounters a character that is not a numeral in the specified radix, it ignores it and all succeeding characters and returns the integer value parsed up to that point. For example, although 1e3 technically encodes an integer (and will be correctly parsed to the integer 1000 by parseFloat()), parseInt("1e3", 10) returns 1, because e is not a valid numeral in base 10. Because . is not a numeral either, the return value will always be an integer.

I think the wording here is slightly misleading and ambiguous. The way it's currently written makes it sound like "If parseInt encounters a character in the radix that's not a numeral..."

What did you expect to see?

I think it would be helpful to reword it as follows and provide an additional example for clarity.

-If `parseInt` encounters a character that is not a numeral in the specified radix, it ignores it and all succeeding characters and returns the integer value parsed up to that point. For example, although `1e3` technically encodes an integer (and will be correctly parsed to the integer `1000` by `parseFloat()`), `parseInt("1e3", 10)` returns `1`, because `e` is not a valid numeral in base 10. Because `.` is not a numeral either, the return value will always be an integer.
+If `parseInt` encounters a character in the input string that is not a valid numeral in the specified radix, it ignores it and all succeeding characters and returns the integer value parsed up to that point. For example, `parseInt('2', 2)` returns `NaN` because `2` is not a valid numeral in binary. Similarly, although `1e3` technically encodes an integer (and will be correctly parsed to the integer `1000` by `parseFloat()`), `parseInt("1e3", 10)` returns `1`, because `e` is not a valid numeral in base 10. Because `.` is not a numeral either, the return value will always be an integer.

Do you have any supporting links, references, or citations?

N/A

Do you have anything more you want to share?

I'd be happy to put in a PR myself.

items.content_html:
MDN URL

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/ReadableStreamDefaultController/close

What specific section or headline is this issue about?

Exceptions

What information was incorrect, unhelpful, or incomplete?

The "Exceptions" section says:

TypeError
Thrown if the source object is not a ReadableStreamDefaultController.

This suggests that errors are not thrown in other cases.

What did you expect to see?

I expect to see that a TypeError may be thrown by this method if the stream is already in the process of closing or closed.

Do you have any supporting links, references, or citations?

https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#rs-default-controller-close

Do you have anything more you want to share?

Similar issues exist for ReadableStreamDefaultController.enqueue and probably methods on WritableStreamDefaultController as well.
